deductions.label: Room-rent and proportionate deduction
deductions.insurerReason: Room category exceeds eligibility. Proportionate deduction applied as per policy.
deductions.ourReading: Kamala stayed in a ₹7,500/day room; the limit is ₹5,000/day, so only two-thirds is eligible. The insurer cut ₹10,000 from room rent and one-third (₹11,600) from nursing and doctor charges. The arithmetic matches the clause.

citations.quote: Room, boarding and nursing expenses are payable up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day for a normal room and up to 2% of the Sum Insured per day for ICU.
Where the room category exceeds eligibility, all associated medical expenses shall be payable in the same proportion as the eligible room rent bears to the actual room rent.

evidence: Final bill page 1: "Deluxe single – ₹7,500 per day × 4 days"
questions: Was a room within ₹5,000/day available when Kamala was admitted? If not, ask the hospital for a written note and ask the insurer to reconsider.

deductions.label: Non-payable consumables
deductions.insurerReason: Non-medical items not payable as per Annexure II.
deductions.ourReading: Gloves, PPE kit and admission kit (₹6,900 on bill page 4) are on the policy's non-payable list, and this policy has no consumables add-on. This deduction looks consistent with the policy.

citations.quote: List I – Items for which coverage is not available: gloves, PPE kit, admission kit, ...

evidence: Final bill page 4: "Gloves, PPE kit, admission kit – ₹6,900"
questions: Check that no medicine was wrongly grouped under consumables.

deductions.label: Other deductions (no reason given)
deductions.insurerReason: "Other deductions" – no reason or clause stated.
deductions.ourReading: The settlement letter shows ₹9,500 without a reason or clause. We could not match it to any bill line or policy rule. You can ask the insurer for an itemised explanation.
evidence: Settlement letter page 2: "Other deductions – ₹9,500" with no remark
questions: Which bill items make up the ₹9,500?
Which policy clause supports this deduction?
